text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Government may ask local authorities to help pay state's part of planned public works programmes halted for lack of public funds.

-- Office furniture and tools manufacturer Strafor Facom chairman Henri Lachmann says in interview he rules out splitting group into two units; speaking after investment funds enter group's capital and call for split.
-- Consumers slightly more optimistic, research centre on savings finds.

-- Only two bidders, BNP and Societe Generale make offers for controlling stake of CIC, parent company GAN may have to recapitalise since offers value CIC around 10 billion francs, while GAN estimated it around 14.5 billion francs.
-- Social Security fund CNAM to present doctors' unions with scheme allowing them to take early retirement at 56 years, in a move to limit their number and save on prescriptions.
-- Eurotunnel shares fell eight percent as they requoted yesterday after debt-restructuring agreement, minority shareholders may launch a referendum on whether to accept settlement.
-- Savings bank grouping Caisses d'Epargne consider a change of status to a mutual bank, to allow for external growth.
-- Brokerage Cholet-Dupont, a subsidiary of Credit Lyonnais CRLPI.PA has bought a 3.37 percent stake in Credit Foncier de France since a state backed buyout offer began.
-- Bouygues public works group posts a 146-million-francs loss for the first half due to depressed roadworks market.

-- Bouygues prepares to become the third telecommunications operator when the French telecommunications market deregulates in 1998, side to side with France Telecom and Cegetel, a joint-venture between Generale des Eaux, intends to tackle local communications market.
